pr_title: drivers: plic: make trigger type default & define registers directly in driver
pr_body:
Removes the trigger type Kconfig option & hardcodes all the registers' offset in the driver instead of getting them from the devicetree since they are strictly defined in the RISCV PLIC specs and aren't something configurable.

See the following for more info:
- https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/62907#discussion_r1332817434
- [RISCV PLIC: Memory Map](https://github.com/riscv/riscv-plic-spec/blob/master/riscv-plic.adoc#2-memory-map)
- Telink B91(added in #35533) [Reference Manual](http://wiki.telink-semi.cn/doc/ds/DS-TLSR9518-E_Datasheet%20for%20Telink%20Multi-Standard%20Wireless%20SoC%20TLSR9518.pdf)
- Andes AX45MP [Reference Manual](https://www.andestech.com/wp-content/uploads/AX45MP-1C-Rev.-5.0.0-Datasheet.pdf)

> [!NOTE]  
> This PR is spined off from https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/62907

Fixes #63466
pr_comments:
> Hi! In general - I feel like the commit messages could use some better justification for the changes we're introducing here. E.g. by stating that these registers in fact are not configurable and their offsets are strictly defined in the specification.

Could you have another look please?

issue_context.title: drivers: intc: plic: edge-triggered interrupt is supported by default, offsets are strictly defined
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
#60851 introduced edge-triggered interrupt that can only be activated only when `CONFIG_PLIC_SUPPORTS_EDGE_IRQ` is enabled, however the RISCV PLIC specs states that the interrupt controller supports both level & edge -triggered interrupt. The support of edge-triggered interrupt in the driver should be supported without the need of an additional Kconfig feature switch, see [RISCV PLIC interrupt gateways](https://github.com/riscv/riscv-plic-spec/blob/master/riscv-plic.adoc#2-interrupt-gateways). 

The current `intc_plic` driver depends on the offsets of the registers to be specified in the devicetree even though they are strictly defined in the RISCV PLIC specs, and should not be configurable, see [RISCV PLIC memory map](https://github.com/riscv/riscv-plic-spec/blob/master/riscv-plic.adoc#2-memory-map). The current pattern in Zephyr also leads to a deviation from Linux's  [sifive,plic-1.0.0.yaml](https://www.kernel.org/doc/Documentation/devicetree/bindings/interrupt-controller/sifive%2Cplic-1.0.0.yaml).

Please also mention any information which could help others to understand
the problem you're facing:
 - Out-of-tree RISCV board with PLIC

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Build application with board that uses PLIC but didn't enable `CONFIG_PLIC_SUPPORTS_EDGE_IRQ`
2. Application that depends on edge-trigger will not work, even though it is supported in the PLIC specs
3. Build PLIC board with wrong register offset
4. Application will not boot properly

**Expected behavior**
Edge-triggered interrupt should be supported by default in PLIC & registers offset should not need to be defined in the devicetree.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: MacOS
 - Toolchain: Zephyr SDK
 - Commit SHA or Version used: d24de87aed9088656c179359d950a8384ac5004a

review_comments:
Hi @ycsin , @cfriedt , @fkokosinski 

Guys, sorry for my late comment on it. I've just stumbled across this hardcoded  offset during the migration to Zephyr 3.5.

I believe hardcoding this offset and making it a default for all the vendors and platforms is a mistake. 
Trigger Type register is not defined in the recent PLIC Spec and so is not compliant with RISC-V Privileged Standard: https://github.com/riscv/riscv-plic-spec/blob/master/riscv-plic-1.0.0.pdf
IMHO this is a miss in the Spec and it results in a situation when all the vendors who support Triggering type configuration implement it in a proprietary way, using the custom offsets and custom codes for the triggering types.

So until it becomes a standard, it would be nice if we leave a room for flexibility here. I think returning PLIC_SUPPORTS_EDGE_IRQ configuration could be a nice option. 

Hope to hear from you. Thanks!

Hi @ycsin , @cfriedt , @fkokosinski , 

I've filed an ticket to track it separately: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/64675
UPD: messed up the "integer literal", sorry :)

I believe we should add a comment here saying that these offsets are taken from the RISC-V PLIC Specification, so that it will be clear in the future that these offsets should be defined here in the driver, and not in the device tree as they are not configurable.
